Twilio Media Streams delivers the caller’s raw audio over a WebSocket, which is the input the voice bridge needs, and CI&T had already integrated it with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic. For contact center workloads that route calls among human agents, Amazon Connect also supports Amazon Nova 2 Sonic.

The architecture uses the following AWS services:

  • Amazon Nova 2 Sonic (through Amazon Bedrock): The speech-to-speech foundation model that powers Tara’s voice conversations. It handles both speech recognition and response generation in a single pass, supporting tool calling for structured data collection during the interview.
  • Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate: A serverless compute engine that runs the voice bridge containers connecting the telephony layer to Amazon Nova 2 Sonic. The voice bridge tasks run continuously across three Availability Zones for high availability.
  • Amazon Aurora Serverless v2: A PostgreSQL-compatible serverless relational database deployed in Multi-AZ configuration. Stores caller profiles, intake responses, qualification results, and session metadata. The serverless scaling of Aurora matches the variable call volume patterns.
  • Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic’s Claude 3 Haiku): Handles structured data extraction from conversation transcripts. After Amazon Nova 2 Sonic generates a transcript, Claude 3 Haiku extracts typed fields (names, dollar amounts, addresses, vehicle details) into the relational schema.
  • Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) with dead-letter queues: Manages asynchronous webhook processing for post-call events, preserving failed messages for retry.
  • AWS WAF, VPC Endpoints, and Application Load Balancer: Security and networking layers that help protect API endpoints, route traffic across Availability Zones, and provide private connectivity to AWS services.

Building and validating the voice agent

The team took a phased approach: validate voice quality first, build the production integration, then expand the questionnaire scope after proving the system worked with real callers.

Validating voice quality for sensitive conversations

Bankruptcy conversations are emotionally charged. Callers are often stressed, hesitant, or embarrassed. The voice agent needs to sound empathetic and natural, not robotic or transactional. Before writing any integration code, the team spent a dedicated week testing the voice quality of Amazon Nova 2 Sonic against several caller scenarios.

The validation covered:

  • Voice quality across caller emotional states (calm, stressed, hesitant, frustrated).
  • Time-to-first-audio latency benchmarks against the previous solution’s over 500 ms baseline.
  • Barge-in and interruption handling: can a caller interject mid-sentence without breaking the conversation?
  • Emotional tone adaptation: does the agent adjust its pace and tone when a caller sounds distressed?

This validation step produced a comparison report documenting the performance of Amazon Nova 2 Sonic against the previous solution across each dimension. The report became the go/no-go gate for proceeding to integration.

Deploying to production with real callers

With voice quality validated, the team built the end-to-end integration over three weeks. The call flow works as follows:

  • A caller dials the Bankruptcy.com number. Twilio’s telephony layer receives the call and opens a WebSocket connection to the voice bridge running on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate.
  • The voice bridge streams audio bidirectionally between the caller and Amazon Nova 2 Sonic. Tara introduces herself, collects consent, and begins the intake interview.
  • After the call, the full transcript feeds into an extraction pipeline powered by Anthropic’s Claude 3 Haiku on Amazon Bedrock. The pipeline extracts the fields from the conversation and stores them in Amazon Aurora.

The full attorney-designed intake can run 15–20 minutes, which is longer than the maximum duration of a single Amazon Nova 2 Sonic streaming session (for the current value, see Getting started with speech-to-speech). The team treated that session duration as a design parameter and implemented the session continuation pattern, an approach that carries conversation context across session boundaries. The voice bridge tracks how long each bidirectional stream with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic has been open. Shortly before the limit, it opens a new stream with the same system prompt and tool configuration and sends the conversation so far as text history. When Tara finishes her current response, the bridge switches the caller’s audio to the new stream and closes the old one, so the conversation continues smoothly for the caller.

The initial deployment covered the existing 13-field intake form, collecting the same data points the web form captured but through natural conversation. This gave the team a production baseline to measure against before expanding scope.

Expanding the intake and lead qualification

With the production pilot running, the team expanded the questionnaire to the full attorney-designed intake over four weeks. This was a significant increase in scope:

  • Over 18 intake categories with conditional branching, where the questions Tara asks depend on the caller’s previous answers.
  • Complex relational data: Vehicles (year, make, model, financing status, monthly payment per vehicle), real estate properties, individual debt line items, multiple employment and income sources, and prior bankruptcy filings.
  • Rules-based lead sorting: Stretto applies attorney-defined rules to each lead, and attorneys make the final decision. Because a voice agent collects richer, conditional data than a static web form, it gives Stretto more flexibility to apply those rules and qualify leads accurately.
  • Lead routing: Qualified leads are routed to bankruptcy practitioners, while callers who do not meet the qualification criteria are directed to alternative resources.

The Amazon Aurora schema expanded to a full relational data model supporting one-to-many relationships. A single caller record might include four vehicles, two properties, and dozens of individual debt line items.

Measuring results and optimizing

The final phase focused on collecting production data and tuning the system based on real caller behavior. The team tracked key performance indicators including call volume, average duration, intake completion rate, profile completeness, conversion rate, and drop-off points.

Insights from production data drove several optimizations: reordering questions to reduce early drop-offs, adjusting conditional branching to collect high-value fields earlier in the conversation, and modifying qualification thresholds based on attorney feedback. The following table shows two key production metrics.

Average call duration (completed calls)~8 min
Data extraction accuracy~96%

Testing for quality and compliance

Deploying a voice agent that handles sensitive financial data requires more than functional testing. The AWS Generative AI Innovation Center (GenAIIC) advisory team guided the development of a comprehensive testing framework spanning four categories:

  • Happy path testing: Complete end-to-end intake interviews with cooperative callers across the full questionnaire. These calls confirm that the over 18 categories collect accurate structured data and that the qualification rules produce correct results.
  • Adversarial testing: Callers who provide contradictory information, change answers mid-conversation, refuse to answer certain questions, or attempt to manipulate the qualification outcome. The agent needs to handle the ambiguity and keep the conversation coherent.
  • Compliance testing: Consent collection, disclosure delivery, and data handling workflows. The team verified that the agent delivers disclosures accurately and collects consent before proceeding, because bankruptcy intake involves sensitive financial information.
  • Barge-in scenario testing: Callers interrupting at various points in the conversation, including during disclosures, mid-question, and during the agent’s responses. Tara should recover without losing context or asking the caller to repeat information.

Responsible AI controls in production

The team treated responsible AI as a production control, not only a testing step. Amazon Nova 2 Sonic includes built-in safety protections, described in the AWS AI Service Card for Amazon Nova 2 Sonic. On top of those, the solution keeps consequential decisions out of the model: lead sorting runs on explicit attorney-defined rules after the call, and attorneys make the final decision. Consent and disclosures are delivered and logged before intake begins, and the adversarial test suite checks that attempts to manipulate the conversation don’t change lead outcomes. Beyond model inference, the solution uses the Amazon Bedrock bidirectional streaming API for real-time audio, tool use for structured data capture during the interview, and private connectivity to Amazon Bedrock through VPC endpoints.

The GenAIIC advisory team also provided guidance on prompt engineering best practices for voice-specific applications, including techniques for managing conversational state across session continuation boundaries and structuring system prompts that maintain consistent agent personality across long interviews.

Results

After roughly three months in production, Stretto reported the following results:

  • Per-lead value: Fully qualified leads with complete intake data are significantly more valuable to bankruptcy attorneys than web form leads, which capture only a few basic fields.
  • Lead conversion: Stretto’s early production results show a 20 percent relative increase in conversion rate compared with the web form, even before the solution has been rolled out broadly across additional districts.
  • Data quality and call length: Stretto reports that Tara extracts structured fields at approximately 96 percent accuracy in its testing, and completed calls average about 8 minutes.
  • Voice solution cost: Stretto reports a 95 percent reduction in per-minute voice cost compared to its previous solution.
“I’m incredibly grateful to the AWS GenAI Innovation Center team. Their expertise helped bring our voice agent, Tara, to life, driving a 20 percent increase in our lead conversion rate.”
— Danya Gordin, Principal AI Architect, Stretto
“As one of the partners in the AWS Generative AI Partner Innovation Alliance, we can confirm that the GenAIIC program is a true catalyst, bringing customers and partners together to solve real problems and deliver business impact. With Stretto, that meant taking a voice agent to production in a matter of weeks and transform the bankruptcy intake process”
— Marcelo Wzorek, Executive Manager, CI&T

Conclusion

Stretto’s journey from web form leads to AI-assisted intake interviews illustrates what becomes possible when voice AI reaches the quality bar for sensitive use cases. By combining the speech-to-speech capabilities of Amazon Nova 2 Sonic with a well-designed architecture on AWS, the team built a voice agent that is natural enough for callers discussing personal financial hardship and cost-effective enough to deliver meaningful savings at scale.

The phased approach, validating voice quality first, deploying a minimal intake to production, then expanding scope based on real-world data, reduced risk at each step. The team built on validated assumptions rather than projections.

If you are exploring AI voice agents for your own use case, here are some resources to get started:

  • Learn about Amazon Nova 2 Sonic and speech-to-speech capabilities.
  • Get started with Amazon Bedrock to access foundation models including Amazon Nova 2 Sonic.
  • Explore AWS Fargate for serverless compute for containers.
  • Learn about the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center for advisory support on your generative AI initiatives.

If you are weighing voice AI for a sensitive, high-value intake process, your AWS account team and the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center can help you scope and build it.

item.title: [Anthropic Claude] Linked billing on the Claude Platform
item.content:encoded:
Today we're introducing linked billing on the Claude Platform in beta. Third-party platforms, such as coding agents and workflow automation tools, can let their end customers pay for Claude API usage without sharing an API key. End customers keep their existing Anthropic billing and set their own spend limits, and platforms get a simpler, more secure way to offer Claude.

A more secure alternative to sharing API keys

Paying for Claude API usage on a third-party platform usually means sharing an API key, which works like a password: anyone who has the key can make requests billed to the customer, so the platform has to keep it safe.

With linked billing, customers link their Claude Platform organization instead, and usage is billed directly to it. No API key changes hands, so platforms have no customer keys to store, encrypt or rotate, and customers’ API keys never leave their organization.

Platforms can see usage for each linked customer. Customers approve each linked platform, set a spend limit, and can unlink at any time.

Linked billing on the Claude Platform

Platforms can offer Claude to customers without building the billing

Linked billing gives platforms a new way to offer Claude to their customers. Platforms send requests, and Anthropic bills the end customers directly. With linked billing, platforms can:

  • Launch faster. Anthropic hosts the approval flow and the billing, so there’s no metering or invoicing to build.
  • Understand usage by customer. Get each linked customer’s request count, token usage and models used in Console, or programmatically with the Usage and Cost Analytics API (beta).
  • Choose who pays. Decide on each request whether the platform or the end customer pays, so platforms can pass Claude API costs to customers or cover some features themselves by product or instance.

Customers get more visibility and control

Customers can easily link to platforms using Anthropic’s hosted flow. They can then draw down from their existing Anthropic commitment, or pay as they go. With linked billing, customers can also:

  • Link once for the whole organization. A Console user with an Owner, Admin, or Billing role approves the link, so it works the same for individual developers and large teams.
  • Set limits for each platform. Customers can set a monthly spend limit for each platform, or a default that applies to each one.
  • See where API spend goes. Console shows spend for each linked platform.
  • Unlink at any time. Customers can unlink directly from Console.

Requests run in the platform’s organization, so settings in the customer’s organization, such as IP allowlists, encryption keys, and data retention, don’t apply.

Platforms that support linked billing today include Asana, ClickHouse, Factory, Gumloop, Harness, Higgsfield AI, Kilo Code, Linear, Major, Mintlify, Omni, OpenArt, Niteshift, Railway, Ramp, Runlayer, Tessera, Tines, and Warp.

Getting started

Linked billing is available today in beta on the Claude Platform. Third-party platforms can add support by creating an app in Console and following the steps in the docs. Claude Platform customers can link their organization from any supported platform, and find platforms that offer linked billing on Claude Marketplace.

“Our customers include some of the largest companies in the world. Linked billing lets them use their own Claude organization in Tessera, with no new keys to manage”

Anirudh Sriram, CTO, Tessera

“Claude is expanding what’s possible with AI, and Tines helps teams across the business build, deploy, and operationalize that work securely, with the visibility and control IT and Security need. Linked billing gives customers a simpler way to bring Claude and Tines together through their existing Claude Platform organization, without sharing API keys, making it easier to control spend and expand AI adoption across the business.”

Charlie Ardagh, Vice President, Strategic Partnerships, Tines

“Engineering teams should have the flexibility to build their software factories with the models and infrastructure they choose. Linked billing makes that easier and more secure, making it seamless for customers to link their own Claude Platform organizations to Warp without having to manage API keys or complex billing arrangements. We’re excited to bring this experience to Warp.”

Zach Lloyd, Founder and CEO, Warp

“Manually copying API keys is inherently insecure. With linked billing, admins can now use their committed Claude spend directly with the Linear cloud coding agent in a click.”

Tom Moor, Member of Technical Staff, Linear

“At Ramp, we want to save customers time and money wherever they work. Linked Billing makes it easier for our customers to use their existing Claude Platform account through Ramp Router, without the hassle of sharing an API key.”

Amanda Carroccio, Director of AI Partnerships, Ramp

“Linked billing with Claude Platform lets developers using Railway Agent focus on getting their applications built and deployed, instead of managing API keys manually. Linking their Claude Platform organization with Railway gives developers a more secure way of accessing their models and spend limits.”

Cody De Arkland, GM, Agent Experience, Railway

“Our customers want to bring AI into more of their work without adding overhead for IT and finance. Linked billing lets them use their existing Claude commitment to power Agentic Work Management in Asana, including AI Studio and AI Teammates, with less setup and spending limits they control as adoption grows.”

Arnab Bose, Chief Product Officer, Asana

“Linked billing makes Claude billing in ClickHouse Cloud turnkey: link your Claude Platform organization, no keys to manage, and Claude API usage is billed to your organization on the terms you already have.”

Ryadh Dahimene, Director of Product Management, AI/ML, ClickHouse

“Linked billing simplifies the onboarding process for our enterprise customers. Instead of creating an Anthropic API key and sharing it with us, an admin links their Claude Platform organization once. We don’t need to hold their key, furthering the security of the integration.”

Leo Tchourakov, Member of Technical Staff, Factory

“Gumloop takes security very seriously, and with linked billing our customers no longer hand their API key to a third party. They link their Claude Platform organization to Gumloop once, and their Claude API usage is billed directly to that organization.”

Rahul Behal, Chief Technology Officer, Gumloop

“Software factories are the next chapter of engineering, and many of our customers are building them with Claude. Using linked billing, they can link their Claude Platform organization to Cosmos by Harness, and Claude API usage in Cosmos is billed to that organization. We’re excited to be supporting linked billing for the Claude Platform.”

Sanjay Nagaraj, SVP of Engineering, Harness

“Our customers look to Claude for agentic capabilities in the tools they use to create. Linked billing lets them link their Claude Platform organization to Higgsfield, with Claude API usage billed directly to their organization. Operational simplicity lets their creative teams focus on what they do best.”

Alex Mashrabov, CEO, Higgsfield AI

“Linked billing means our customers link their Claude Platform organization and everything just works. We get to spend our time building instead of managing credentials.”

Kyle Finken, Engineer Manager, Mintlify

“Niteshift orchestrates cloud coding agents with full-stack dev environments. As agent usage grows in volume and scope, our customers are increasingly focused on both cost control and security. Linked billing allows them to set a monthly spend limit and keep their billing relationship with Anthropic, without sharing long-lived API keys.”

Sajid Mehmood, CEO & Co-Founder, Niteshift

“Claude is a core model in OpenArt’s agentic layer. With linked billing, our customers can link their Claude Platform organization to OpenArt with no API key to share, and Claude API usage in OpenArt is billed directly to that organization. That makes OpenArt simpler to adopt across their teams.”

Coco Mao, Co-founder and CEO of OpenArt

“Linked billing with Claude Platform lets customers link their Claude organization to Omni without sharing an API key. Alongside Omni’s own usage tracking, they can trace Claude token usage back to Omni for better auditability.”

Marc Dupuis, Director of Product, Omni

“Runlayer works with enterprises at the frontier of AI, and we’re excited to be supporting linked billing on the Claude Platform. No API key to share means one less attack vector.”

Andy Berman, CEO, Runlayer

“Our customers include some of the largest companies in the world. Linked billing lets them use their own Claude organization in Tessera, with no new keys to manage”

Anirudh Sriram, CTO, Tessera

“Claude is expanding what’s possible with AI, and Tines helps teams across the business build, deploy, and operationalize that work securely, with the visibility and control IT and Security need. Linked billing gives customers a simpler way to bring Claude and Tines together through their existing Claude Platform organization, without sharing API keys, making it easier to control spend and expand AI adoption across the business.”

Charlie Ardagh, Vice President, Strategic Partnerships, Tines

“Engineering teams should have the flexibility to build their software factories with the models and infrastructure they choose. Linked billing makes that easier and more secure, making it seamless for customers to link their own Claude Platform organizations to Warp without having to manage API keys or complex billing arrangements. We’re excited to bring this experience to Warp.”

Zach Lloyd, Founder and CEO, Warp

“Manually copying API keys is inherently insecure. With linked billing, admins can now use their committed Claude spend directly with the Linear cloud coding agent in a click.”

Tom Moor, Member of Technical Staff, Linear

“At Ramp, we want to save customers time and money wherever they work. Linked Billing makes it easier for our customers to use their existing Claude Platform account through Ramp Router, without the hassle of sharing an API key.”

Amanda Carroccio, Director of AI Partnerships, Ramp

“Linked billing with Claude Platform lets developers using Railway Agent focus on getting their applications built and deployed, instead of managing API keys manually. Linking their Claude Platform organization with Railway gives developers a more secure way of accessing their models and spend limits.”

Cody De Arkland, GM, Agent Experience, Railway

item.title: [Meta Llama] Muse Is Now Available in Australia: The World’s First Person…
item.description: Full title: Muse Is Now Available in Australia: The World’s First Personal AI Agent Built for Everyone
item.content:encoded:
Meta

Takeaways

  • Muse is a personal AI agent. It doesn’t just answer questions, it actually does the work. It helps people stay on top of things, takes tasks and projects off their plate, and turns long-term goals into action plans.
  • Muse is available in Australia from today, with local connector experiences across creativity, shopping, property, fitness and entertainment rolling out progressively.
  • Meta built Muse from the ground up to be a safe, secure, private, and widely available personal AI agent.
  • Each person stays in control of their Muse and decides how much access it gets.

Following our global announcement of Muse, we are excited to share that Muse is now available in Australia.

What Muse can do in Australia

Connectors are a big reason Muse can do so much. People in Australia can connect their Muse to apps and services they already use, such as Gmail, Google Calendar, Instagram and OpenTable, so it can help them manage emails, coordinate schedules, draw on saved content and make a restaurant reservation—all part of getting everyday tasks done.

Early local connector partners in Australia include Canva, Domain, Kogan, MECCA, Officeworks, realestate.com.au, SWEAT, ShopBack, and Ticketek. Connector features will roll out progressively, with some experiences becoming available after launch. Canva, the global all-in-one visual communication platform that empowers anyone to design, is also available as a connector for Muse users around the world.

As these experiences become available, you could ask Muse to to design any visuals or content you need with Canva, explore property listings on Domain and realestate.com.au, or work towards fitness goals with SWEAT. You could also buy great value electronics and appliances through Kogan.com, beauty products through MECCA, school and office supplies through Officeworks, or tickets through Ticketek. With ShopBack, you could compare prices and earn cashback and rewards on flights, hotels and shopping.

More ways to use Muse

Real time conversations with your Muse are now possible on mobile, web or Mac. With voice, you can talk through an idea with your Muse and let it take shape without worrying about the exact prompt. Just tap the phone icon in the top-right corner to start talking.

Spaces, a custom experience you create inside Muse by describing your idea, is now also available. Spaces can help you get things done, have a little fun, or give your creative projects a home, whether it’s a shopping hub, school dashboard, wedding planner, or trip planner to name a few ideas.

Built to be private, safe and secure

Making this technology work for everyone requires careful design and engineering to operate more safely. That’s where most of the effort on this project went and this post explains our approach in detail. Muse runs on Muse Secure VM, a dedicated computer in the cloud that securely stores the data and credentials for the services you connect, while keeping passwords and payment methods out of the agent’s view. You choose what your Muse can access, and it checks with you before sensitive actions such as sending an email or making a purchase.

Will Easton, Managing Director, Meta Australia and New Zealand, said: “With the festive season coming up, the timing couldn’t be better. From finding and buying the perfect gift to planning and booking a holiday, Muse is designed to take work off Australians’ plates. As local experiences roll out, familiar services will make Muse even more useful in everyday life. And people stay in control, including choosing what Muse can access and approving purchases before they happen.”

Muse is available in Australia on iOS, Android, and muse.ai, a Mac app, and coming soon to AI glasses. It’s free for most of what people need, with subscription plans for people who want to do more.
